verdict.rationale: Every SKILL.md must include a `name` and `description`. Codex reads that metadata to decide when to load a skill, and the skill creator asks authors what the skill does and when it should trigger. That makes self-description built into the format. However, trigger conditions are not a separately required field, and activation is a model decision driven by free-text descriptions, so how predictable it is remains unproven. Missing for 10: a mandated, structured activation/trigger field, evidence that activation actually matches the documented description, and independent hands-on corroboration of predictability.

support.subject: As a developer, every skill documents what it does and when it activates, so I can predict my agent's new behavior before it surprises me

citations.quote: The creator asks what the skill does, when it should trigger, and whether it should stay instruction-only or include scripts.
ChatGPT and Codex start with each skill's name and description, then load the full `SKILL.md` instructions when they decide to use that skill.
